models_evaluated: deployed breast AI platform: tomosynthesis-based malignancy score
deployed breast AI platform: synthesized-2D-based malignancy score

links.outcome: Cancers receiving a negative (low) AI score at the cohort-derived threshold
links.effect: 30 cancers were negative by the tomosynthesis output; 25 had no mammographic correlate on re-review, and breast density did not fully explain this. Authors advise against using a low AI score alone to downgrade a suspicious finding.
links.quote: Of 30 cancers negative by the tomosynthesis output, 25 had no mammographic correlate on re-review, and breast density did not fully explain this pattern.

unlisted_practices: Testing whether co-reported AI outputs from the same platform (tomosynthesis-based vs synthesized-image-based) are interchangeable
Assessing the incremental value of AI scores beyond clinical-radiological assessment using logistic models and decision-curve analysis
Targeted AI-masked re-review of cancers missed by AI output

screen.reason: Evaluates the practice of interpreting co-reported malignancy scores from a deployed breast AI platform, examining score interchangeability, decision-support value over clinical-radiological assessment, and safety implications of downgrading findings.

primary.practice: comparing co-reported AI outputs and incremental decision support
